text:
linda: FYI acme-x on Dedicated reported sudden 429s + some 401s this morning during a long-context batch run. They say it started ~09:05 PT and lasted ~15m.
akshat: any clue if this is our autoscale lag or kv eviction churn?
linda: ticket includes logs. customer says requests spike with ~150k token contexts, mostly chat completions. We saw a burst of evictions in the kvcache metrics around the same time.
esteban: can you paste the logs? even a small snippet helps.
linda: sure — here's the tail from the inference host around the incident window:
```
[09:05:12] kvcache: evict start slab=3 free=128B target=64MB
[09:05:13] kvmgr: eviction_count=1294 tenant=acme-x long_ctx=true seq=150k
[09:05:14] serve: request=abc123 tenant=acme-x model=rwkv-13b variant=q4f token_len=149800 latency=1200ms
[09:05:15] auth: token-validate duration=30ms status=200
[09:05:16] autoscale: scale_up_start reason=kv_pressure current_replicas=4 desired=8
[09:05:20] serve: request=def456 tenant=acme-x status=429 retry-after=10
[09:05:23] auth: token-validate duration=200ms status=401
[09:05:25] billing: charge_attempt id=chg_5xx status=failed
```
kevin: interesting the auth 401s line up with heavy eviction events. when the cache thrashes we stall inference threads, which delays auth token refreshes and can surface as 401s upstream.
akshat: customer mentioned a billing spike alert too. billing-bot, did we create an overage charge?
billing-bot: noticed increased token usage for tenant acme-x 2026-01-18 09:05-09:20 UTC, provisional estimate +18% relative to baseline. No automatic invoice yet.
support-engineer: from the support side they reported retries with backoff but their client circuit breaker triggered and then immediately retried, creating a tight loop. That made the burst even worse.
esteban: repro steps I've got so far: 1) send mix of long-context chat streams (140k-160k tokens) across ~300 concurrent sessions 2) include a small fraction of token-heavy system prompts (prefixes) 3) client retries immediately on 429s with no jitter
linda: i also ran a quick curl to the endpoint from our lab to simulate:
```
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.redwood.api/acme-x/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @longctx.json &
done
```
akshat: thanks — that reproduces eviction storm. Observed kvcache slab compaction not keeping up; fragmentation increases after repeated evictions. Our allocator then spends more CPU compacting which slows request handling.
kevin: immediate mitigations we can try for customer: 1) enable tenant-level prefix caching (cache pinning) for hot prefixes 2) increase kvcache memory for that Dedicated pool temporarily 3) adjust autoscale to a more aggressive scale_up for kv_pressure events 4) ask them to implement exponential backoff on retries
esteban: we should also toggle slab compaction tuning: set `kv.compact_threshold=0.25` and bump `kv.compact_interval` down to 30s in the Dedicated pool for acme-x — that'll trade CPU for fragmentation reduction.
akshat: agree. I'll push a temporary config to the Dedicated tenant: `kv.mem_reserve=1.5GB` and `autoscale.kv_pressure.scale_up_factor=2` for the next 2h.
linda: customer okayed a maintenance window and will accept small perf jitter while we test.
sre-bot: deploy started: apply config to pool dedicated-acme-x-1 by akshat at 09:42 PT. See runbook: https://console.redwood/ops/runbooks/kv-evict
billing-bot: note — increasing memory & replicas may change billing; reached out to acme-x billing contact for approval.
support-engineer: after the changes they reported 429s dropped to near-zero within ~6 minutes, and auth failures cleared. They still see slightly increased latency (~200ms) for some requests but far fewer errors.
esteban: we should schedule a postmortem with the tenant to review workload shaping and long-context usage patterns. Also recommend they split ultra-long system prefixes out of hot request paths when possible.
kevin: long-term ideas: - smarter kv placement to isolate heavy longctx prefixes - tenant QoS to cap eviction rate per-tenant - faster incremental compaction kernel for slabs
akshat: i'll roll back the aggressive scale-up after the window; will leave `kv.mem_reserve` up for 1 hour. Notes in the ticket.
linda: thanks team. I'll update the customer ticket with our actions + suggested client changes (backoff, reduce immediate retries, prefix pinning).
sre-bot: deploy complete: config applied successfully at 09:48 PT.
kevin: open action items: akshat follow up on rollback, esteban draft postmortem, support-engineer confirm billing consent. I'll add to #incidents calendar.
linda: closing loop with acme-x now. :thumbsup:
